summary: A red-and-white steel pillar light on the St. Lawrence at the Saguenay mouth, which replaced the river's last lightship and survived a two-day storm at Christmas 1966.

notes_for_editor: Tower history and the 1966 storm rest on Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted, paraphrased) plus the Register; Fr Wikipedia (lead only) names Lightship No. 4 at the station 1960-63 and gives 36 hours/5 a.m.; unverified. Keeper dates in 1966 are approximate (spring return and departures from LHF). Federal heritage designation (2008, FHBRO 11796) in the record could not be read from Parks Canada's page and is omitted from the story. Cloutier says 1906-1956 for No. 7 while the Department report says 1905; Cloutier's PDF is two-column so quotes were matched from the extracted text.
